BR.compilation: From 5 Mar 1999 onwards Central Bank target, money market (SELIC) overnight rate; from 1 Jul 1996 to 4 Mar 1999: Central Bank official rediscount rate; from 4 Jun 1986 to 30 Jun 1996: official market intervention rate, representative rate.

AR.compilation: From 10 July 2025 onwards: no policy rate adopted; from 22 July 2024 to 9 July 2025: liquidity absorption rate for treasury bills; from 18 December 2023 to 21 July 2024: Overnight Reverse Repos Interest Rate; from 6 January 2022 to 17 December 2023: 28-day Liquidity Bills (LELIQ) interest rate; from 21 January 2020 to 5 January 2022: weighted average interest rate of minimum term LELIQ issued at the last auction process; from 1 October 2018 to 20 January 2020, average interest rate of the accepted offers for the liquidity bills; from 8 August 2018 to 30 September 2018: 7 days liquidity bills interest rate; from 2 January 2017 to 7 August 2018, median of the repo rate corridor; from 16 December 2015 to 1 January 2017: interest rate in BCRA bills (LEBACs), 35 days LEBAC auction; from 29 Jan 2014 to 15 Dec 2015: CB issues, 3 months; from 11 Sep 2009 to 28 Jan 2014:7-day reverse repo operations; before 10 Sep 2009, refer to https://data.bis.org/topics/CBPOL

AU.compilation: From 2 Aug 1990 onwards: cash rate target; from 23 Jan 1990 to 1 Aug 1990: middle of the cash rate target range; from 7 Apr 1976 to 22 Jan 1990: interbank overnight cash rate.

CL.compilation: From 1997 onwards: official monetary policy rate.

CN.compilation: From 20 Aug 2019 onwards: Loan Prime Rate  (1 year): from 1 Jan 1996 till 19 Aug 2019: Official lending rate (1 year).

CA.compilation: From 1 Jun 1994 onwards: Central Bank target, overnight rate; from 27 Jul 1960 to 31 May 1994: official bank rate.

CH.compilation: From 13 June 2019 onwards SNB Policy rate; From 1 Jan 2000 to 12 June 2019 mid-point of the SNB target range; from 1 Jan 1946 to 31 Dec 1999: discount rate.

HR.compilation: From 4 Jan 1993 to 1 Sep 2002: interest rate on money market interbank loans. From 2 Sep 2002 to 31 Dec 2022: interest rate on money market interbank deposits. From 1 Jan 2023 onwards: the series is discontinued as Croatia joined the euro area.

GB.compilation: From 3 Aug 2006 onwards: official bank rate; from 6 May 1997 to 2 Aug 2006: repo rate; from 20 Aug 1981 to 5 May 1997: minimum Bank of England Band 1 dealing rate; from 16 Oct 1972 to 19 Aug 1981: minimum lending rate; from 1 Jan 1946 to 15 Oct 1972: bank rate.

GR.compilation: From 1 Jan 2001 onwards: the series is discontinued as Greece joined the euro area; from 28 Mar 1997 to 31 Dec 2000: overnight deposit facility - 1st tier; from 2 Jan 1995 to 27 Mar 1997: overnight intervention (mid) rate; from 1 May 1956 to 01 Jan 1995: discount rate of the Bank of Greece; from 1 Jan 1941 to 30 Apr 1956: no data available; from 30 Mar 1841 to 31 Dec 1940: rate imposed on trade advances at the head offices of the National Bank of Greece (NBG) in Athens and the discount rate by the Bank of Greece sourced from Lazaretou (2014). Between 1956 and 1993, the day the rate becomes effective is assumed to be the first day of the month.  Before 1956, whenever the day of changes is not available, it is set to the end-of-month.

ES.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Spain joined the euro area; from 14 May 1990 to 31 Dec 1998: the main policy rate was the marginal interest rate of the ten day auctions of Bank of Spain certificates; from 4 May 1983 to 13 May 1990: marginal interest rate of day-by-day monetary adjustment loans; from 14 Sep 1977 to 3 May 1983: marginal interest rate of overnight monetary adjustment loans; from 1 Jan 1945 to 13 Sep 1977: the rediscount interest rate.
ES.source_ref: Bank of Spain, Bank for International Settlements

FR.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as France joined the euro area; from 4 Jan 1982 to 31 Dec 1998: the rate corresponds to the repo rate; from 5 Jul 1973 to 3 Jan 1982: the rate corresponds to the repo rate on call for tenders, firm purchases or repos before purchases on public and private bills of 1st category ("taux des interventions effectuées par la Banque de France sur appels d'offres, achats fermes ou pensions avant achats, effets publics et effets privés à court terme de 1ère catégorie"). Whenever multiple rates were available for a given period, the rate with the shortest maturity has been selected; from 20 Jan 1945 to 4 Jul 1973: the rate was the official discount rate set by the Bank of France.
FR.source_ref: Bank of France, Bank for International Settlements

DE.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Germany joined the euro area; from 1 Jan 1985 to 31 Dec 1998: repo rate; from 1 Jan 1979 to 31 Dec 1984: Lombard rate; prior to 31 Dec 1978: discount rate.
DE.source_ref: Deutsche Bundesbank, Bank for International Settlements

DK.compilation: From 1 April 1992 onwards: interest rate of the certificates of deposits; from  2 Jan 1979 to 31 Mar 1992: official discount rate; from 1 Jan 1946 to 1 Jan 1979: discount rate.

JP.compilation: From 24 Sep 2026: the BOJ encourages the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 1.25 percent; From 17 Jun 2026 to 23 Sep 2026: the BOJ encourages the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 1.00 percent; From 22 Dec 2025 to 16 Jun 2026: the BOJ encourages the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 0.75 percent; From 27 Jan 2025 to 21 Dec 2025: the BOJ encourages the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 0.50 percent; From 1 Aug 2024 to 26 Jan 2025: the BOJ encouraged the UOCR to remain at around 0.25% ; From 21 Mar 2024 to 31 July: the BOJ encouraged the UOCR to remain at around 0 to 0.1 %; from 21 Sep 2016 to 20 Mar 2024: the BOJ set the guideline for market operations which specifies a short-term policy interest rate at minus 0.1% and a target level of 10-year JGB yields at around 0%. Short-term policy interest rate; from 4 Apr 2013 to 20 Sep 2016: no policy rate; from 5 Oct 2010 to 3 Apr 2013: the BOJ encouraged the UOCR to remain at around 0 to 0.1%; from 19 Dec 2008 to 4 Oct 2010: the BOJ encouraged the UOCR to remain at around 0. %; from 31 Oct 2008 to 18 Dec 2008: the BOJ encouraged the UOCR to remain at around 0.3%; before 30 Oct 2008, refer to https://data.bis.org/topics/CBPOL

KR.compilation: From 7 Mar 2008 onwards: Bank of Korea base rate; from 6 May 1999 to 6 Mar 2008: target overnight call rate(base rate).

IS.compilation: From 21 May 2014 onwards: Central Bank term deposit rate; from Sep 2009 to 20 May 2014: average of the current account rate and the maximum rate on 28-day certificates of deposits; from 1 Apr 2009 to Sept 2009: current account rate; from 2 Mar 1998 to 31 Mar 2009: 7 day collateralised lending rate.

IT.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Italy joined the euro area; from 1 Jan 1992 to 31 Dec 1998: the official discount rate and the rate for fixed-term advances were respectively the lower and upper limits of the so-called corridor of official rates; from 1 Jan 1945 to 31 Dec 1991: the official interest rate of Bank of Italy was applied to the discounting of banks' ordinary portfolios.
IT.source_ref: Bank of Italy, Bank for International Settlements

IN.compilation: From 3 Apr 2001 onwards: official repo overnight rate; from 1 Jan 1946 to 2 Apr 2001: oank rate.

ID.compilation: From 19 Aug 2016 onwards: 7 day reverse repo rate; from 5 Jul 2005 to 18 Aug 2016: official base rate (BI rate).

AT.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Austria joined the euro area; from 2 Sep 1996 to 31 Dec 1998: tender fixed rate; from 6 May 1985 to 1 Sep 1996: GOMEX rate; from 18 Sep 1979 to 5 May 1985: Lombard rate with surcharge; from 24 Jan 1979 to 17 Sep 1979: Lombard rate; before 24 Jan 1979: discount rate.
AT.source_ref: Central Bank of the Republic of Austria, Bank for International Settlements

NO.compilation: From 11 Jun 1993 onwards: official deposit facility rate; from 3 Mar 1986 to 10 Jun 1993 official credit facility rate.

NZ.compilation: From 17 Mar 1999 onwards: Official market intervention representative rate, official cash rate; from Jan 1985 to 16 Mar 1999: overnight cash rate.

MY.compilation: From 26 Apr 2004 onwards: overnight policy rate; from 1 Jan 1998 to 25 Apr 2004: 3 month intervention rate; from 3 Nov 1995 to 31 Dec 1997: 3 month interbank rate.

NL.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Netherlands joined the euro area; prior to 31 Dec 1998: the main interest policy rate corresponds to the fixed advance rate set by the De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).
NL.source_ref: De Nederlandsche Bank, Bank for International Settlements

MK.source_ref: National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia

BE.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Belgium joined the euro area; from 1 Feb 1991 to 31 Dec 1998: the rate was the current account advances rate; from 1 Jan 1945 to 31 Jan 1991: the rate was the official discount rate set by the National Bank of Belgium.
BE.source_ref: National Bank of Belgium, Bank for International Settlements

MX.compilation: From 21 Jan 2008 onwards: Central Bank target, money-market overnight rate; from 3 Nov 1998 to 20 Jan 2008: bank funding rate.

MA.compilation: From 01 Jan 2001: interest rate, 7-day advances (Taux directeur)

RU.compilation: From 13 Sept 2013 onwards: official key rate; from 1 Jan 1992 to 12 Sep 2013: official refinancing rate.

SA.compilation: From 1 Jan 2000 onwards: official market repo rate.

RS.compilation: From 1 Sept 2006 onwards: Central Bank policy rate; from 1 Jan 1997 to 31 Aug 2006: Central Bank discount rate.

PL.compilation: From 26 Feb 1998 onwards: official 7 day central bank bill yield; from 1 Jan 1993 to 25 Feb 1998: Lombard rate.

PT.compilation: From 1 Jan 1999 onwards: the series is discontinued as Portugal joined the euro area; from 19 Aug 1965 to 31 Dec 1998: the daily series is derived from the historical series published by Banco de Portugal; from 1 Jan 1945 to 18 Aug 1965: the official discount rate is sourced from the Bank for International Settlements. The discount rate is the interest rate charged by Banco de Portugal to credit institutions in credit provision operations.
PT.source_ref: Banco de Portugal, Bank for International Settlements

PH.compilation: From Jan 1986 onwards: Official market intervention representative rate, liquidity providing.

TR.compilation: From 20 May 2010 onwards: 1 week official repo rate; from 20 Feb 2002 to 19 May 2010: Central Bank overnight borrowing rate.
TR.source_ref: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

US.compilation: From 19 Dec 1985 onwards: mid-point of the Federal Reserve target rate; from 1 Jul 1954 to 18 Dec 1985: US Fed Funds effective rate.

SE.compilation: From 1 Jun 1994 onwards: Central Bank fixed repo/reversed repo rate; from 30 Jan 1987 to 31 May 1994: marginal rate; from 1 Jan 1946 to 29 Jan 1987: discount rate.

TH.compilation: Offical market intervention representative rate, liquidity providing repo rate.
